name: Hotkeys

hero.title: You have written this `keydown` listener before. It was the last time.
hero.lede: `useHotkey('mod+s', save)` is ⌘S on a Mac and Ctrl+S everywhere else, skips text fields, stops the browser's own save dialog and unregisters when the component goes. Sequences like `g i`, scopes for the editor, and a list of every shortcut for your help dialog come with it.

why.title: The details you forget at 11 pm.

items.title: Typing is not a shortcut
items.text: Shortcuts stay quiet while focus is in an input, textarea, select or contenteditable. Opt back in with `enableOnInputs: true`, or only for text inputs with `['input']`.

items.title: `mod` means the right key
items.text: ⌘ on macOS, Ctrl on Windows and Linux, from one string. `?` fires on Shift+/, so the help shortcut works on every layout that has a question mark.

items.title: Scopes that stack
items.text: `useHotkeyScope('editor')` turns the editor's Ctrl+Z on while the editor is mounted. Activation is reference-counted, so two editors on one page do not switch each other off.

items.title: A miss costs one lookup
items.text: Dispatch is bucketed by key. A keypress that is not a shortcut, which is most of them, touches one `Map` and leaves, however many shortcuts you registered.

before.label: React, by hand
before.caption: Skip inputs, guess the platform, prevent the default, remember the cleanup. In every component that needs a shortcut.

after.label: with @pyreon/hotkeys
after.caption: Same behaviour. Inputs skipped, default prevented, removed on unmount, listed in your help dialog.
after.code:
import { useHotkey } from '@pyreon/hotkeys'

useHotkey('mod+s', () => save(), { description: 'Save' })

comingFrom.title: `$mod+KeyK` becomes `mod+k`.
comingFrom.after:
import { useHotkey } from '@pyreon/hotkeys'

useHotkey('mod+k', () => openPalette())
useHotkey('g i', () => goToInbox())
comingFrom.note: Sequences use the same space-separated form. `preventDefault` is on by default; pass `preventDefault: false` to let the browser act too.

comingFrom.title: Scopes without a global `setScope`.
comingFrom.after:
import { useHotkey, useHotkeyScope } from '@pyreon/hotkeys'

useHotkey('mod+s', () => save())

// in the editor component:
useHotkeyScope('editor')
useHotkey('ctrl+z', () => undo(), { scope: 'editor' })
comingFrom.note: hotkeys-js has one active scope at a time. Here any number of scopes can be on together, each held for as long as a component that asked for it is mounted.

demo.text: Click inside the box to give it focus, then try the shortcuts. Toggle the editor scope to see scoped keys switch on and off.

items.name: `useHotkey`
items.text: Registers on setup, unregisters on unmount. `target` takes an element ref for panel-local keys.

items.name: Sequences
items.text: `g i`, Gmail and vim style: the next key must follow within a second.

items.name: Comma lists
items.text: `'ctrl+s, mod+p'` binds one handler to several combos.

items.name: `useHotkeyScope`
items.text: Reference-counted scopes; `enableScope` / `disableScope` for code outside components.

items.name: `once` and `ignoreRepeat`
items.text: Fire once and unregister, or ignore auto-repeat while a key is held.

items.name: `enabled: () => …`
items.text: Gate a shortcut on a signal: no re-registering when the condition flips.

items.name: `trigger('g i')`
items.text: Run the bound action from a command palette or a test. Returns how many handlers fired.

items.name: `getRegisteredHotkeys()`
items.text: Every shortcut with its scope and description, ready for a "?" help dialog.

items.name: `getHotkeyConflicts()`
items.text: Finds `ctrl+s` and `control+s` bound twice in one scope, even when the strings differ.

recipes.title: A help dialog that lists itself
recipes.text: Give each shortcut a description. The list that `?` opens reads the registry each time it opens, so it never drifts from what is bound.

recipes.title: Shortcuts that only work in the panel
recipes.text: Escape closes the panel only while focus is inside it. The listener is shared and removed with the last binding.

api.title: Hooks, a registry and a parser.

limits.title: Text fields win by default
limits.text: A shortcut does not fire while the user types. If ⌘S should save from inside a textarea, pass `enableOnInputs: ['textarea']` or `true`.

limits.title: Build server help panels from config
limits.text: Registration is a no-op on the server, so `getRegisteredHotkeys()` is empty during SSR. Render a static list there, or the live one after mount.

limits.title: Sequences fire on keydown
limits.text: `g i` cannot use `event: 'keyup'`; registration throws a clear error if you try.

limits.title: On native, keep it literal
limits.text: iOS and Android lower `useHotkey` with a literal shortcut and a handler that does not read the event. A computed shortcut, a comma list or a handler reading `e.key` warns by name and is dropped there.

faq.q: Does it prevent the browser default?
faq.a: Yes, by default, which is what you want for ⌘S and ⌘K. Pass `preventDefault: false` for a shortcut that should let the browser act as well.

faq.q: What about keyboard layouts and IME input?
faq.a: Matching uses the key the layout produces, so `?` fires on Shift+/. With Alt held it falls back to the physical key, so `alt+s` works on a Mac, where Option+S types ß. Keystrokes inside an IME composition never match, so typing Japanese or Chinese does not trigger shortcuts.

Against tinykeys, hotkeys-js and mousetrap: dispatch on a hit 1.7–7.5×, a miss 6.0–118× with 12 and 48 bindings, register plus teardown 1.17× vs tinykeys and 9–14× vs the other two. One run, bun, author-run; the record lists no loss.

faq.q: Do I need to clean up?
faq.a: Not with `useHotkey`: it unregisters on unmount. `registerHotkey` returns an unregister function for code outside components.

benchmarks.rival: vs tinykeys 4, hotkeys-js 4, mousetrap 1.6 · bun/JavaScriptCore, 12 and 48 bindings
benchmarks.h: A key that is not a shortcut: up to 118× cheaper.
benchmarks.p: Most keypresses are typing, not shortcuts, so the miss path is the one that runs all day. Pyreon buckets shortcuts by key; a miss is one lookup. Ranges cover the three rivals and both binding counts. No loss or tie is recorded.

sources.claim: hotkeys vs tinykeys/hotkeys-js/mousetrap: hit 1.7–7.5×, miss 6.0–118× (12 and 48 bindings), register+teardown 1.17× / 9–14×; no loss
Key-bucketed dispatch: a miss is one Map lookup; one shared listener per (target, event type)
Defaults: preventDefault true, enableOnInputs false (input/textarea/select/contenteditable), scope global
mod+s fires on Ctrl+S (non-Mac UA), ignored inside an <input>, sequence g i, ? on Shift+/, scoped ctrl+z only after enableScope, trigger returns 1, unregister works
getHotkeyConflicts finds mod+s and control+s as one conflict
registerHotkey is a no-op on the server
keyup is rejected for sequences with a clear error
useHotkey target accepts a getter, resolved after mount
Native: literal useHotkey lowers to SwiftUI .keyboardShortcut / Compose key handler; computed shortcut, combo list, reading the event warn and drop
Rival before-code typechecks (tinykeys 4.0.1, hotkeys-js 4.1.2, React 19 types)
